newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Avis Europe says happy with share float result.
newsitem.headline: Avis Europe says happy with share float result.

text.p: Car rental firm Avis Europe, majority owned by Belgian car importer and distributor D'Ieteren, said on Wednesday it was happy with the result of its oversubscribed share float, priced at 124 pence per share.

"The flotation will enable us to improve our financial strength through access to additional funds and to invest in the further expansion of the business," Avis Europe chairman and chief executive Alun Cathcart said.
Avis said conditional dealings in the shares would start today, with unconditional dealings starting on the London Stock Exchange on April 4.
A total of 215 million shares will be issued, raising an estimated 267 million pounds sterling, with a net 161 million going to the company, Avis said in a statement.
A total of 582 million shares will be in issue following the offer which, at a price of 124 pence per share, values total issued ordinary share capital of the firm at 722 million pounds sterling.

Avis said that in view of the weight of oversubscription of the share offer, retail investors would receive 725 shares in respect of the first 1,000 pounds of their demand plus 10 percent of the difference between their demand and 1,000 pounds.
As part of the offer, D'Ieteren has granted Merrill Lynch an option to buy 30 million existing shares in Avis, the leading car rental company in Europe.
If this is exercised in full, D'Ieteren's share of Avis Europe will fall to 56.9 percent. D'Ieteren has said it intended to remain a long-term strategic sharholder in Avis Europe.
Avis Europe serves more than five million customers a year through some 2,400 locations.
